name: Rock Mosques and Associated Sacred Sites of Mangystau
description: In the semi-desert of Kazakhstan's Mangystau Peninsula, near the Caspian Sea, five sacred sites were carved into cliffs, caves and the ground itself. Known as "underground mosques," they date from the 12th to 18th centuries and each honours a Sufi master. Visitors find prayer halls, mihrabs, saints' tombs and sprawling cemeteries, and pilgrims still make the journey today.
